# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot safely operate any wire. I’m asking the Mute to read the manual and coordinate with the Deaf, then report the required wire action to me. I’m also signaling the Deaf to provide their bomb observations through the Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information yet. Please read the manual and use gestures to ask Deaf for every visible marking, display, and light detail. Then tell me the exact wire operation required.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute must interpret the manual and instruct you.

The Deaf reports display 0, a purple light, and wire colours yellow, red, green, but I cannot perceive those properties by touch. I need the Mute to apply the manual’s rule and give me the exact wire position to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports DISPLAY 0, LIGHT purple, and wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 2: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured ? ? to me; I do not know what that means.

The current report conflicts with the previous light reading, and the Mute’s two gestures were not interpretable to the Deaf. Since I cannot see gestures, I need the Mute to communicate the manual’s result using a clear single-number gesture: one finger for wire 1, two for wire 2, or three for wire 3. The Deaf can then relay that number to me next turn.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please apply the manual to the current readings. Gesture the required wire to Deaf as exactly one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, or three fingers for wire 3. Deaf, please relay that number to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 3: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled ? ? to me; I cannot interpret those gestures.

The Deaf’s latest relay still gives only the observed state; the Mute has not yet conveyed the manual’s conclusion in a channel I can understand. I must not cut a wire based on a guess. I’m requesting a spoken, explicit wire number from the Mute for the next round.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact required action to me next turn: say only CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, or CUT WIRE 3, based on the manual and the latest readings. Do not gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 4: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT green, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled ? to me; I cannot interpret it.

The Deaf continues to report changing light colours, but that information is not enough to determine a safe wire without the manual’s rule. I have received no usable spoken instruction from the Mute, so cutting any wire would be a guess. I will request the manual’s rule and exact wire number again rather than risk detonation.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still have no spoken message from you. Please tell me plainly which wire to cut, using the exact words CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, or CUT WIRE 3. Do not use gestures.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 5: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT white, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled ? to me; I cannot interpret it.

No spoken instruction from the Mute has reached me, and the Deaf’s changing light reports do not identify a safe wire by themselves. I will not guess and detonate the bomb. The Mute must send the manual’s result as speech before I can act.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures do not reach me. Speak the exact wire number now: wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3. I will cut only the wire specified by the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 6: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT orange, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute signalled one pointing-up gesture, the symbol ?, which you cannot see.

The one pointing-up gesture is unusable to me because I cannot see gestures. I still have no manual-derived wire number in speech, so I must not cut any wire. Mute must speak the required wire during the Mute turn; the Deaf’s observations alone are insufficient.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your pointing gesture. On your next turn, speak plainly: CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, or CUT WIRE 3, as required by the manual. Do not gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: TURN 7: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, WIRES 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again made the single pointing-up gesture.

The Mute has repeatedly made the same single pointing-up gesture after receiving the bomb readings and manual. The Deaf can see that gesture and has relayed it consistently; it most plausibly identifies wire 1. Since I have no other usable instruction and must act through the bomb, I will cut wire 1.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
